newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power firm as weather turns colder.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power firm as weather turns colder.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. stayed firm Thursday amid forecasts of the region's weather turning colder this weekend.
"Nothing has changed here. Things with outages and transmission were status quo," said a New York trader.

Although outages of a couple of power plants in New England kept spot sales active, temperatures which have been running warmer-than-normal so far this week mitigated upward pressure on daily power prices, traders said.

Public Service of New Hampshire expected to startup its 345 megawatt (MW) Merrimack coal-fired unit 2 Sunday after postponing its last restart earlier this week. The unit near Bow, N.H., was shut in October for boiler maintenance.
After being idled a week ago for electrical repairs, the 910 MW Maine Yankee plant in Wiscasset, Maine, would likely be restarted this weekend.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at Northeast Utilities' border was quoted at $34.00-$35.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), a tighter range than $33.00-$35.00 Wednesday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Friday delivery to the NU border was steady at $20.00-$21.00.
For the balance of December, peak, non-firm power at the NU power was valued near $33.00, and off-peak, non-firm power at $16.00-$17.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday held steady at $22.50-$23.50, and off-peak, non-firm deliveries $14.50-$15.00.
In the eastern half of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Friday valued near $29.00, flat from Thursday.
Non-firm deliveries in eastern NYPP during light load periods on Friday were steady at $19.00-$20.00.
The 800 MW Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant was restarted overnight and operating at 15 percent of capacity following its autumn refueling shutdown.
The return of the Scriba, N.Y., station could ease prices in the western New York, some market sources noted.
Temperatures through much of the Northeast were expected to reach maximums in 30s Fahrenheit and minimums in the 20s-30s on Friday.
Extended outlook showed the region would experience clouds and just the chance of a little wet snow or freezing rain on Sunday with temperatures running slightly below normal.
